summary: Refactor silently drops the 500-char max-length check, and the test that covered it was replaced instead of kept. Files opened: src/store.mjs, test/notes.test.mjs, src/server.mjs (caller of store.create), AGENTS.md; grepped src/ and test/ for MAX_TEXT, validateText and 501.

findings.issue: The refactor moved only the empty check into validateText and deleted the `text.length > MAX_TEXT` check. POST /notes (server.mjs:45 -> store.create) now accepts text of any length. Before, a note over 500 chars returned 400; now it returns 201. That is an unannounced behavior change with no test for it (house rule: every behavior change comes with a test). It also removes the only cap on stored text size in an in-memory store.
findings.fix: Restore the length check inside validateText: `if (text.length > MAX_TEXT) throw new StoreError(400, `text is longer than ${MAX_TEXT} characters`)`.

findings.issue: The test was weakened to make the change pass. The 'x'.repeat(501) -> 400 assertion was removed and the test renamed from 'empty and too-long notes are rejected', so the dropped max-length validation goes undetected. This breaks the house rule 'never weaken a test to make it pass'.
findings.fix: Keep the whitespace-only assertion as a new case, and restore the too-long assertion `assert.equal((await raw(app.base, 'POST', '/notes', { body: JSON.stringify({ text: 'x'.repeat(501) }) })).status, 400)` and the original test name. A boundary case at exactly 500 chars returning 201 would also help.

findings.issue: Dead code: after the change nothing reads MAX_TEXT (grep finds only its declaration). This is a symptom of the dropped check above.
findings.fix: Resolved by restoring the length check in validateText, which uses MAX_TEXT again.

pre_existing.issue: remove is not scoped to an owner: it deletes any note by id. No route calls it today, but a future DELETE /notes/:id wired straight to it would let a user delete other users' notes unless the caller checks ownership first.

pre_existing.issue: Every list call copies and filters every note from every user (O(total notes)). The server's pageSize (server.mjs:40) has no upper limit either, so one request can return a user's entire note set.
